land.text: Raska, held by Vukan and Marko as zupans under the Doclean king Bodin until Vukan 'became independent' in 1091 or 1092

predecessors.note: The Grand Principality page: 'In 1091 or 1092, Vukan became independent, taking the title of Grand Prince'; infobox 'Established: 1091'. Bodin installed Vukan and Marko in Raska (Bodin page, cited in the duklja dossier).

land.text: Stefan Nemanja's Serbia: 'Grand Prince Stefan Nemanja (r. 1166-1196) gained full independence and united almost all Serbian lands'; the dossier's last land is the 1152 outline held for 1169-1187 plus the Neretva region and the Doclean land annexed in 1186

successors.note: The state continues: the Grand Principality page's infobox runs it to 1217 (Stefan the First-Crowned crowned King, 1217). Extended after review from 1168 to 1187, the year before Cliopatria's Kingdom of Serbia row starts (1188), so that Nemanja's 1169-1187 land is drawn and the 1186 annexation of Duklja has a living counterpart. The dissolve at 1187 is a hand-over to the kingdom-of-serbia dossier (eu-18, not written yet), not the end of the state: if that dossier takes 1217 as its start instead, this one should run to 1217 and the 1187 dissolve be replaced by one at 1217.

capitals.name: Ras (Stari Ras)
capitals.note: Nemanja 'gathered supporters at Ras' in 1166/1167 and held the assembly near Ras in 1196; the Grand Principality page names no capital and Niš became his capital by 1189 (Nemanja page). The point is the gazetteer's Stari Ras. Reviewer eu-18-b: point moved to the Stari Ras page's coordinates (43°7′42″N 20°24′56″E, 'some 10-11 kilometers west of modern-day Novi Pazar'); the gazetteer's 20.6E lay east of every shape's bbox. Extended to 1187 with the dossier; Nis is Nemanja's 'new capital' only in 1189 (Nemanja page).

rulers.name: Vukan
rulers.title: Grand Prince
rulers.note: 'In 1091 or 1092, Vukan became independent'; the Grand Principality infobox lists 'Vukan 1083-1112'; 'he is believed to have died in ca. 1112, succeeded by his cousin' Uros (Uros I).

rulers.name: Uros I
rulers.title: Grand Prince
rulers.note: Desa page: 'the Grand Prince of Serbia from c. 1112 to 1145'.

rulers.name: Uros II
rulers.title: Grand Prince
rulers.note: Desa page: 'The eldest son Uros II succeeded their father in 1145' (the same page also has him ruling alone 'from 1140' until the battle at the Tara river, c. 1150); Grand Principality page: 'In 1153, Desa ousted Uros II'.

rulers.name: Desa
rulers.title: Grand Prince
rulers.note: First reign 'c. 1155' on the Desa page (infobox); Manuel I 're-instated Uros II in 1155, deposing Desa'. Desa appears in Venetian charters from 1150 as prince of Duklja, Travunija and Zahumlje and was co-ruler with Uros after the Tara river.

rulers.name: Uros II (restored)
rulers.title: Grand Prince
rulers.note: Desa page: Manuel 're-instated Uros II in 1155'; Grand Principality page: 'In 1161-62, Uros II was briefly replaced by Beloš'; Desa page: 'In early 1160s, Uros II was deposed being replaced by Beloš'.

rulers.name: Belos
rulers.title: Grand Prince
rulers.note: Grand Principality page: 'briefly replaced by Beloš, who then returned to his office in Hungary and Croatia'; Desa page: he 'soon resigned in favor of Desa, with Manuel I's approval'.

rulers.name: Desa (second reign)
rulers.title: Grand Prince
rulers.note: Desa page infobox 'Reign: 1162-1166', predecessor Beloš, successor Tihomir.

rulers.name: Tihomir
rulers.title: Grand Zupan
rulers.note: Desa page: 'Manuel put Tihomir on the throne in 1166'; Nemanja page: in January 1166 Tihomir was recognised as Grand Zupan and Nemanja received Ibar, Toplica and Dubocica. Ends in 1166 where Nemanja's reign begins (Grand Principality page 'r. 1166-1196'); his overthrow is dated 1166/1167 (Nemanja page, Grand Principality page: expelled 1167) or 1168 (Nemanja page, Byzantine reaction in autumn 1168).

rulers.name: Stefan Nemanja
rulers.title: Grand Prince
rulers.note: Reigned 1166-1196 (Grand Principality page infobox; the rest in the kingdom-of-serbia dossier, which is not written). Reign years of Uros I to Desa are the Desa page's; the Grand Principality page itself gives no years for them.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1091-1093: Vukan's independence is 'in 1091 or 1092' (infobox 'Established: 1091'); Cliopatria starts in 1094. The 1094 shape is carried back. The page has no area.

19.9 thousand km2 for 1094-1138. The page says the principality encompassed 'various neighbouring regions, including territories of Raska' and names modern Montenegro, Herzegovina and southern Dalmatia; no borders or area are given, so the Cliopatria core around Raska stands. Vukan raided Byzantine Kosovo from ca. 1090.
19.9 thousand km2 for 1139-1151, the same outline; the pages opened date no territorial change in these years (Beloš held the Hungarian office of comes palatinus in 1145). Unverified: page budget.

28.9 thousand km2, +9 thousand to 41.85N (Skadar): Duklja, Travunija and Zahumlje, of which Desa was 'dux' in a charter of 1150 (page). The shape adds them two years after the charter and treats Duklja's core as Serbian; the Duklja dossier keeps its own shape and contests the zone from 1150, so the overlap is drawn as contested. Holds to 1168; after Nemanja's accession in 1166 the shape is unchanged in Cliopatria (Nemanja page: Ibar, Toplica, Dubocica; Kotor 1166/1167).

correction.text: Nemanja's land 1169-1171: the 1152 outline carried forward (Ras, Ibar, Toplica, Dubocica, Duklja contested, Kotor from 1166/67); Cliopatria has no shape for 1169-1187

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Grand Principality row ends in 1168 and its Kingdom of Serbia row starts in 1188, so nothing is drawn for 1169-1187 although the state runs to 1217 (infobox). The Nemanja page: after the Byzantine move of autumn 1168 he submits and is restored as Grand Zupan; no territorial change is dated for 1169-1171. The 1152 outline is carried forward. No area on the page.

union.text: the Neretva region (the lower Neretva valley)

correction.text: Nemanja's land 1172-1187: the 1152 outline plus the Neretva region annexed with a part of Zeta in 1172; Skadar (1184) lies inside the outline, and the Doclean remainder annexed in 1186 is inside it too

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 1172 'a part of the then Zeta and the Neretva region' (Nemanja page); 1184 Skadar; 1186 Duklja 'in its entirety' (Duklja page) - the Doclean outline of 1126 lies wholly inside the 1152 shape (31 of 31 cells), so only the Neretva circle adds land. The contest with Duklja is drawn 1150-1186. Held to 1187; the kingdom-of-serbia dossier takes over in 1188.

ledger.note: 1091: Vukan becomes independent and takes the title of Grand Prince. 'In 1091 or 1092, Vukan became independent, taking the title of Grand Prince'; infobox 'Established: 1091'; he had been regional governor under Bodin (c. 1082) and raided Byzantine Kosovo from about 1090.

1150: Desa appears as dux of Travunija and Zahumlje. 'In 1150, Desa was mentioned in a charter as dux of Duklja, Travunija and Zahumlje.' Cliopatria draws these lands in 1152; the page does not say how Desa came to hold them. Reopened: the Desa page has him 'instated as co-ruler along with Uros' after the battle at the Tara river and 'mentioned in Venetian charters from 1150 as a Prince of Duklja, Travunija and Zahumlje' (rule over these 'ca. 1149 to 1162'); still no page says from whom he took them, so the counterpart stays nobody.

region.text: Duklja's core, contested between Raska and the Doclean princes

ledger.note: 1150: the same charter names Desa dux of Duklja. 'By 1166 much of Duklja was under Raska' (Duklja page); Nemanja's annexation of Duklja in 1186 lies beyond this dossier. Zone: Duklja's core.

1166: Stefan Nemanja gains the principality and begins the Nemanjic line. 'Grand Prince Stefan Nemanja (r. 1166-1196) gained full independence'; in January 1166 Tihomir was recognised as Grand Zupan and Nemanja received Ibar, Toplica and Dubocica.

1166/1167: Nemanja conquers Kotor. 'Nemanja conquered Kotor, then gathered supporters at Ras and overthrew Tihomir'; Tihomir, Stracimir and Miroslav were 'defeated, and expelled to Byzantium in 1167' (Grand Principality page). Reopened: the Nemanja page later calls it 'Byzantine Kotor' (attacks after the 1171 break with Byzantium), and the Kotor page has the city autonomous as the 'Commune of Cattaro' 1003-1185, 'conquered in 1185 by Stefan Nemanja' and then in the Grand Principality 1185-1217. The two pages disagree (1166/67 against 1185) and the first conquest was apparently not held; counterpart left as the commune, year kept from the Nemanja page.

region.text: the Neretva region (the lower Neretva valley), taken with a part of Zeta

ledger.note: 1172: Nemanja takes a part of Zeta and the Neretva region. 'The following year, Nemanja attacked the Byzantine vassal, Prince of Zeta Radoslav and on that occasion annexed to his country a part of the then Zeta and the Neretva region' (the year after the 12 March 1171 confiscation of Venetian property; the conflict ends with his surrender to Manuel). The page gives no year of its own and no extent; the 25 km circle on the lower Neretva is the dossier's reading, and the Zeta part lies inside the 1152 outline already contested with Duklja. The Duklja dossier has no 1172 loss. Nemanja is restored as Grand Zupan by Manuel.

1184: Nemanja takes Byzantine Skadar. 'The following year, Nemanja launched an offensive on the southeastern Adriatic coast and conquered Byzantine Skadar' (after his great offensive of 1183, allied with Bela III; the page never writes 1184). Cliopatria's 1152 outline already reaches Skadar, so this is mostly a confirmation inside it. byzantine-empire has no 1184 loss in this batch.

region.text: Duklja, annexed 'in its entirety' by Nemanja

ledger.note: 1186: the contest for Duklja ends in Nemanja's annexation. Duklja page: Nemanja 'annexed Duklja in its entirety after defeating the last Doclean prince - Mihailo'; infobox 'Conquered by Grand Principality of Serbia: 1186/9'. Matches great-principality-of-duklja /ledger/10.

region.text: Duklja, annexed 'in its entirety' by Nemanja

ledger.note: 1186: the last Doclean land passes to Nemanja. Duklja page: 'annexed Duklja in its entirety'; 'By 1166, much of Duklja was occupied by Rascia'. Matches great-principality-of-duklja /ledger/11 (loss to this slug). Nemanja page: silent on Duklja and Mihailo.

union.text: the Neretva region (the lower Neretva valley)

region.text: the principality's land at the hand-over: the 1152 outline, the Neretva region and the annexed Duklja

ledger.note: 1187: dossier boundary, a hand-over to kingdom-of-serbia, whose Cliopatria row starts in 1188. Not the end of the state: the Grand Principality page's infobox has 'Established: 1091', 'Disestablished: 1217' (Stefan crowned King in 1217).

wars.name: Vukan's raids on Byzantine Kosovo
wars.outcome: Vukan 'began raiding Byzantine territory in the vicinity of Kosovo in ca. 1090'; no border change is recorded on the page.
wars.note: The Bodin page (opened for the Duklja dossier) cites conflicts with Alexios in 1091 and 1093-1094.

wars.name: Byzantine-Hungarian wars of the 1120s and 1150s
wars.outcome: 'In ca. 1127, a Byzantine-Hungarian war broke out'; 'In 1151, Manuel I declared war on Hungary'; Desa ousted Uros II in 1153. No Serbian border change dated.
wars.note: The page's role for Raska is as an ally of Hungary and a Byzantine tributary 'up to 1180'; details not on the page.

wars.name: Nemanja against his brothers and Byzantium
wars.outcome: Nemanja overthrows Tihomir (1166/1167), Tihomir, Stracimir and Miroslav are expelled to Byzantium in 1167; in autumn 1168 Byzantine forces move against Nemanja, who submits to Manuel I; in 1172 Manuel restores him as Grand Zupan after he surrenders at Nis.
wars.note: The 1172 restoration lies beyond this dossier's last year.

wars.name: Nemanja against Radoslav of Zeta and the Byzantine break of 1171-1172

zones.text: the Neretva region and a part of Zeta

wars.outcome: Nemanja, closer to the Venetians after the 1171 confiscation, attacks Prince Radoslav of Zeta and annexes a part of Zeta and the Neretva region; the conflict ends with his surrender to Manuel at Nis and his restoration as Grand Zupan.
wars.note: The page gives no year for the surrender or the annexation; the 'following year' after 1171 is 1172.

wars.name: Nemanja's offensive on the Adriatic coast
wars.outcome: 1183: a great offensive on Byzantium allied with Bela III (Bela takes Belgrade, Nis and Serdica); 'the following year' Nemanja conquers Byzantine Skadar and besieges Dubrovnik; peace with Dubrovnik in September 1186.
wars.note: The page names 1183 and 1186 but not 1184.

certainty.note: The pages give no borders, only named lands; 'recognizing the supreme overlordship of the Byzantine Empire, up to 1180' (page) makes the southern and Kosovo frontiers approximate throughout. 1169-1187 (added after review) is equally soft: Cliopatria has no shape, and the 1152 outline plus the Neretva circle is the dossier's reading of the Nemanja and Duklja pages.

sources.title: Grand Principality of Serbia
sources.note: Identity, infobox (1091, 1217), Vukan, Desa 1150, Byzantine suzerainty to 1180, Nemanja; no infobox area.

sources.title: Stefan Nemanja
sources.note: 1166-1172: Tihomir, Kotor, the Byzantine submission; 1184 Skadar; 1196. Reread after review: 1172 Zeta and Neretva, 1183-1184 offensive and Skadar, 1186 peace with Dubrovnik, Nis capital 1189.

sources.title: Desa, Grand Prince of Serbia
sources.note: Reign years of Uros I, Uros II, Desa and Beloš; Tihomir 1166; 1150 charters. Read after review.

sources.title: Duklja
sources.note: 1186 annexation by Nemanja, "in its entirety", Mihailo; infobox 1186/9. Read after review.

sources.title: Kotor
sources.note: "Conquered in 1185 by Stefan Nemanja"; Commune of Cattaro 1003-1185. Read after review.

notes: Page budget (1-2) spent on the Grand Principality article and Stefan Nemanja. The Duklja page (opened for great-principality-of-duklja) supplies 'Raska, Zahumlje and Bosnia probably broke away after 1090'. Not one state with principality-of-serbia: Wikidata Q1311990 is shared by the Vlastimirovic principality (780-960), the Vukanovic Grand Principality (1091-) and the Cliopatria row 'Serbia'; the 130-year gap, dynasty, capital (Ras) and Byzantine rule 971-1018 make them different states, kept as separate dossiers. BOUNDARY (revised after review): the page's state runs to 1217; this dossier now runs to 1187 (new keyframes 1169 and 1172, events 1172, 1184, 1186, dissolve 1187 as a hand-over) because Cliopatria's Kingdom of Serbia row starts in 1188. The kingdom-of-serbia dossier (eu-18, not written) should open with a hand-over from this slug in 1188 and carry the state to 1217 and beyond; the colour agent should give the two one colour (family balkans). If that dossier starts in 1217 instead, extend this one to 1217. Nemanja's 1172 Zeta and Neretva annexation, the 1183-1184 offensive (Skadar 1184) and the 1186 annexation of Duklja are now in the ledger. Rulers 1112-1166 come from the Desa page (the Grand Principality page gives the order and events but no reign years; the Desa page itself has Uros II in 1140/1145-c. 1150 and 1153 differently). Byzantine overlordship of Raska ('up to 1180') is recorded on the suzerain's side only (byzantine-empire dossier) and is not written here. Cliopatria has no shape for 1169-1187. Gazetteer names needed: Raska is present as 'Rascia'; Travunija, Ibar valley, Toplica, Dubocica not checked.
